title: Stalk localization of explicit affine tensor coordinates
statement: Let R,A,R',A' be commutative rings with R-algebra structures on A,R' and a structure map A tensor_R R' to A'. Let phi_g':A to A' and phi_f':R' to A' be its restrictions and assume their spectrum square is cartesian. Let M be an A-K-flat unbounded complex, K a quasi-coherent derived object on Spec A, e:Q(tilde M) isomorphic to K, L=Lg'^*K quasi-coherent, and assume the canonical pullback counit on tilde M is invertible. Let m be any base-derived tensor cohomology model and i any integer. Define U and a by [def-pc-affine-base-change-tilde-coordinates] and its canonical target coordinate. For every prime p of A', the localization U_p is additively isomorphic, by lU, to the source of the canonical stalk arrow r=affineBaseChangeIntoPullback on tilde M and e. For all x in U_p, affineDerivedCohomologyStalkIso applied to the localized a(x) equals r(lU(x)). This only compares the prescribed module arrow at stalks; it asserts no global direct-image presentation or mate square.

proof.text: Apply exists_affineBaseChangeOrdinaryStalkComparison to obtain the localized source equivalence and the square ending in cohomology of ordinary tensor pullback. Factor the prescribed module arrow as a0 followed by the canonical target cohomology coordinate, and use functoriality of LocalizedModule.map. Apply affineTensorPullbackHomologyStalkIso_coordinates and the ordinary square. The resulting composite is definitionally affineBaseChangeIntoPullback.
